title: Does a trend filter improve the top-10 checklist?
summary: Compare the original top-10 portfolio with a market filter, a stock filter, and both together. The selection rules stay fixed across the four variations.
note: Exploratory follow-up. The 2022 onward period was already inspected in the parent study.

title: Ranking the checklist: all passers or the top 10?
summary: A quarterly momentum ranking narrows the checklist to ten stocks. Compare it with the original equal-allocation portfolio and inspect the selection mechanics.
note: Exploratory follow-up. The later-period results are not an untouched holdout.

title: The checklist, four ways to build a portfolio
summary: Compare risk-sized positions, an SPY cash allocation, equal allocation, and a trailing-only checklist. Forward-estimate proxies and their limitations are documented alongside the results.

title: Traveling Trader: the rules put to the test
summary: An overview of the dip ladder, fundamentals checklist, EMA trade, timing rules, and put hedge. Each major experiment has a detailed report in this library.

title: Buying the dip versus a monthly investment
summary: Test cash reserves deployed at index drawdowns against regular monthly purchases. S&P 500 and QQQ results cover several reserve rules and rolling investment windows.

title: The 9/21 EMA pullback trade
summary: Portfolio backtests and an event study of the EMA pullback setup, with exits on either the first or second close below the 21-day EMA.

title: Does the fundamentals checklist select better stocks?
summary: Test the valuation, profitability, leverage, and cash-flow rules as quarterly screens, including a separate 2011 to 2015 holdout.

title: VIX spikes, summer seasonality, and midterm years
summary: Event studies of the market-timing rules across the S&P 500 and QQQ, with unconditional returns and alternate calendar windows for comparison.

title: What does a standing index-put hedge cost?
summary: Compare put budgets, strike prices, pricing assumptions, and seasonal hedging rules in a simulated S&P 500 portfolio.

title: Tom Nash's quality screen, with and without rule 7
summary: Operating-margin and free-cash-flow versions of the checklist, with sector exclusions, blend and sleeve portfolios, and a separately labelled post-hoc data cleanup.

title: Testing the Nash rules before building the portfolio
summary: An individual-rule study across holdout, in-sample, and later periods, followed by portfolio construction tests using the stated selection criteria.

title: Episodic pivot: does the result survive nearby settings?
summary: Vary the gap threshold, holding period, and SPY filter around the corrected strategy. Inspect the neighboring parameter grid and the report's robustness checks.

title: Episodic pivot, after correcting liquidity and exits
summary: Re-run the strategy with liquidity measured before the signal and a corrected partial-sale rule. Compare three exits, standalone positions, SPY overlays, and cash reserves.

title: Episodic pivot: idle cash, T-bills, and an SPY overlay
summary: A closer look at the SPY-filtered strategy's exposure, trade concentration, and use of idle capital, with cash, T-bill, and SPY-overlay variations.
note: Historical experiment using the original liquidity and exit rules. See the corrected episodic-pivot report for the subsequent fixes.

title: Episodic pivot: increasing risk per trade
summary: Keep the signals fixed and vary the equity risk and position cap. Compare return, drawdown, cash constraints, and the largest trade losses.
note: Historical experiment using the original liquidity and exit rules. A later report documents the corrected strategy.

title: Episodic pivot: gaps, neglect, and exit rules
summary: The initial earnings-gap experiment. Compare gap thresholds, the neglected-stock condition, and three exit rules across the same test periods.
note: Initial experiment. Later research corrected the signal-day liquidity test and the day-three partial-sale rule.

title: Do market filters help the breakout strategies?
summary: Six market filters applied to Qullamaggie breakouts, Minervini VCPs, and episodic pivots. Open positions keep their exit rules while filters gate new signals.

title: Minervini's trend template and VCP
summary: A volatility-contraction setup following the trend template, tested with two exit approaches. Includes signal counts and low-volume breakout handling.

title: Qullamaggie breakout: when to enter
summary: Compare pivot entries, strong closes, volume confirmation, and intraday entries. Stop-limit variations and the shorter intraday-data window stay in the same report.

title: Qullamaggie breakout: when to exit
summary: Replay the original breakout entries under different stops, targets, time exits, and moving-average trails. The report distinguishes trade-level and portfolio-level results.

title: Qullamaggie breakout: 10-day or 20-day trail?
summary: The original breakout study, comparing two moving-average trails and a worst-case entry-day assumption for each.

title: S&P 500 GARP Index: self-managed or ETF?
summary: S&P's growth-at-a-reasonable-price index rebuilt from its published rules and checked against SPGP's holdings and returns. Compares running it yourself with owning the ETF, before and after tax, from December 2015, with an approximate run from 2007.

title: MSCI USA Quality GARP (iShares GARP): self-managed or ETF?
summary: MSCI's growth-at-a-reasonable-price index explained step by step, tested on MSCI's official daily series back to 2002, with a rules-based rebuild to cost out running it yourself. Compared with the S&P 500 GARP study, SPY and growth benchmarks, before and after tax. The returns are MSCI's own; holdings, self-managed costs and taxes come from a rebuild that lacks MSCI's forecast and universe data, so they are approximate.

title: The Turtle Trading rules on six ETFs
summary: The 2003 Original Turtle Trading Rules run on SPY, QQQ, gold, silver, oil and long Treasuries from 2006, long and short, as written and with gross exposure capped at 2x and 1x. Compared with SPY and QQQ buy-and-hold, with trade statistics, crisis behaviour and cost sensitivity.

title: Turtle variations: without SPY and TLT, and long only
summary: Two follow-ups to the six-ETF Turtle test: long and short on QQQ, gold, silver and oil only, and System 2 long only. Each as written, capped at 2x and 1x gross exposure, and with smaller units, compared with SPY, QQQ and the original runs.
note: Both variations drop what lost money in the first study's results, so they were chosen with hindsight. The report checks the choice against 2006-2015 alone.

title: Nick Radge's Weekend Trend Trader: two stop rules
summary: The weekly breakout system (20-week high, 30% rate of change, index above its 10-week average, a 40% trailing stop that tightens to 10%) on US stocks from 2016. The stop as the book describes it against a recomputed stop that loosens again. The book gives no rule for choosing between signals, so random selection runs 200 times and is compared with momentum rankings and SPY.
note: The fixed-ranking and median random runs are listed as variations; the headline is the distribution of random selections in the report.

title: Weekend Trend Trader on the S&P 500 and MidCap 400
summary: The same rules and both stop variants, limited to stocks in the S&P 500 or S&P MidCap 400 at the signal week (point-in-time membership from the S&P 500 change log, and Wikipedia's S&P 400 list checked against archived IJH holdings). Random selection 200 times per universe, each index alone and both together, compared with the all-stocks study, SPY and IJH.
note: Follow-up to the all-stocks study. The S&P 400 history is reconstructed, not an official constituent file; the report shows how closely it matches IJH.

title: A QuantifiedStrategies-style Weekend Trend Trader on the Russell 3000 and S&P 900
summary: A reconstruction of the version QuantifiedStrategies published (18% on the Russell 3000, 20-23% on the S&P indexes since 1990): the same entries, a 40% trailing stop that never tightens, 10 positions of 10% and no costs. Run on point-in-time Russell 3000 members (from archived iShares holdings) and S&P 500 + MidCap 400 members, from 2016, with random selection 200 times, a 3-month ranking, and WTT as written on the same universes.
note: QuantifiedStrategies' exact rules are members-only; the exit and ranking here are inferred from what they disclose.

title: WTT and the QS-style version before and after tax
summary: Both versions rerun on point-in-time Russell 3000 and S&P 500 + MidCap 400 universes, with a ranking chosen in advance (12-month momentum), dividends, top federal taxes paid from the account, SPY taxed the same way, vol-matched SPY on margin, and risk measures against SPY, plus random selection and robustness checks.
note: Taxes are an accounting layer: the trades are the same with and without them. Top federal rates, no state tax.

title: Rayner Teo's moving-average pullback, before and after tax
summary: His 50/200 EMA pullback as a fixed daily rule: the third pullback into the 50-day EMA area after two completed tests, a hammer or bullish engulfing trigger, 1% risk. All eight combinations of the rules his articles disagree on (trend filter, stop, exit), on point-in-time S&P 500 + MidCap 400 and Russell 3000 members from 2016, with dividends, taxes paid from the account, SPY taxed the same way, vol-matched SPY, risk measures against SPY, trade statistics (expectancy, payoff, profit factor, SQN, excursions), an every-signal study, random selection and robustness checks.
note: Discretionary parts of his method (which average the market respects, what counts as a test, how strong a rejection candle must be) had to be fixed as mechanical rules; the report lists each judgement call and moves it one notch in the robustness checks.

title: Rayner Teo's moving-average pullback on SPY and QQQ
summary: The same rules and eight variants as the stock study, run on the two index ETFs from their first trading days (SPY from 1994, QQQ from 2000), before and after tax. As specified (third touch only) the rule traded 13 times in 33 years; two looser touch rules, added after counting and reported as departures, give up to 104 trades. Includes trade statistics, each ETF alone, an event study of the bounce against an ordinary uptrend day, taxes, vol-matched SPY and robustness checks.
note: The looser touch rules were added after seeing the signal count.
